column1: # Label taxonomy — the single source of truth for this repository's issue labels.
# Format: name <TAB> color (6 hex digits, no #) <TAB> description.
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. `scripts/sync-labels.sh` applies this file to
# GitHub; `scripts/check-issue-triage.sh` gates that every open issue carries a valid
# combination. AGENTS.md §10: the rule lives in a failing command, not in prose someone
# has to remember.
# Four namespaces, four different questions, answered independently:
#   kind/    what the issue IS          exactly one   mandatory
#   area/    where it lands             one or more   mandatory
#   status/  what it is waiting on      exactly one   mandatory
#   gate/    what shipping without it costs (#206)    at most one, optional
# The multi-dimensional, prefixed shape is the practice of every tracker that outgrew a flat
# label list — kubernetes/test-infra `label_sync` (kind/, area/, sig/, priority/, triage/,
# lifecycle/), rust-lang/rust (C-, A-, T-, S-, P-), bevyengine/bevy (C-, A-, S-, D-, X-). One
# colour per namespace so the label bar reads as columns rather than as confetti.
# Deliberately absent — each of these would be a second, drifting ordering:
#   priority/*   `gate/*` already answers "does the release wait on it", and the milestone
#                answers "which release". A third axis maintained by hand would contradict
#                the other two within a month.
#   lifecycle/*  the k8s stale->rotten->closed bot is a defence against a backlog nobody
#                reads. Here the equivalent is `status/parked` with a wake-up trigger
#                written in the body: an issue is parked *by decision*, never by neglect.
#   status/in-progress   assignees and the linked PR already carry it, mechanically.
# kind/ — what the issue IS. Exactly one. The question it answers: what kind of work, if
# any, closes this? `investigation`/`design`/`decision` are the three shapes of "not code
# yet", kept apart because they are unblocked by different things: a measurement, a written
# design, a maintainer call. The same three-step ladder golang/go runs as NeedsInvestigation
# -> NeedsDecision -> NeedsFix.
kind/bug
column3: Behaviour, or an API, contradicts its documented or advertised contract

column1: kind/feature
column3: A new capability, behind new API or new machinery

column1: kind/enhancement
column3: Improves existing behaviour — performance, ergonomics — with no new capability

column1: kind/cleanup
column3: Internal quality, hygiene or metadata; no observable behaviour change

column1: kind/docs
column3: Documentation only — no code change closes it

column1: kind/investigation
column3: The answer is not known yet: measure, reproduce, instrument. Closes with evidence

column1: kind/design
column3: The solution space is open. Closes with a written design or RFC, not with code

column1: kind/decision
column3: Options are framed; a maintainer call is what is missing. Lands in ARCHITECTURE.md §7

column1: kind/epic
column3: Umbrella over sub-issues. Carries no work of its own

column1: # area/ — where it lands. One or more. The five crate values mirror ARCHITECTURE.md §2's
# map exactly, so the label set cannot drift from the workspace; the seven cross-cutting
# values name the concerns that span crates. Widening this list means updating
# ARCHITECTURE.md §2 in the same change, exactly as scripts/check-domain-purity.sh requires.
area/rsos
column3: The ordered map, fingerprint and canonical encoding

column1: area/rbsr
column3: The range-based set-reconciliation algorithm and its refinement policy

column1: area/lww-register
column3: Domain types — Entry/State, Timestamp/HLC, the Clock and Persistence ports

column1: area/gossip
column3: Transport, authentication, replay protection, discovery

column1: area/reconcile
column3: The facade — ReplicatedMap, ReadReplicaMap, Config, wiring

column1: area/wire
column3: The on-the-wire and on-disk formats — compatibility is at stake

column1: area/security
column3: Threat model, cryptography, key handling

column1: area/persistence
column3: Snapshots, durability, recovery

column1: area/observability
column3: Metrics, tracing, operational signals

column1: area/perf
column3: Throughput, latency, memory, and the benchmarks that measure them

column1: area/release
column3: Packaging, semver, CI, publication mechanics

column1: area/meta
column3: The repository itself — its docs, its tracker, its agent instructions

column1: # status/ — what it is waiting on. Exactly one. This is the field that decides whether an
# issue is pickable *right now*, so it is the one worth keeping honest.
status/needs-triage
column3: Not yet classified. The default on anything new; no other status may accompany it

column1: status/needs-investigation
column3: Blocked on evidence — a measurement or a reproduction, not a decision

column1: status/needs-decision
column3: Understood and framed; blocked on a maintainer call

column1: status/ready
column3: Understood, unblocked, and actionable as written

column1: status/blocked
column3: Blocked by another issue, named in the body

column1: status/parked
column3: Deliberately not now. The body MUST state what would wake it up

column1: # gate/ — what shipping 1.0.0 without it costs. At most one; absence means "not a gate".
# Repo-specific, and the reason this namespace exists at all: #206 §2 already defines these
# three classes and maintains them as hand-written tables in two files. Tables drift — on
# 2026-08-13 five rows were stale within a day. A label is queryable and cannot fall out of
# sync with itself.
gate/a-breaking
column3: Non-additive: deferring past the tag costs a 2.0.0 (#206 §3)

column1: gate/b-claim
column3: A claim the 1.0.0 release makes would be false on day one (#206 §4)

column1: gate/c-mechanics
column3: Cannot ship, be found, or be verified without it (#206 §5)

column1: # Meta — GitHub gives these two exact names special treatment (repository "good first
# issues" surfacing, the contribute API), so they keep their canonical spelling and stay
# outside the namespaces.
good first issue
column3: Scoped, self-contained, and reachable without repository context

column1: help wanted
column3: Maintainers would take a contribution here
